title: Waves and Sound

standard_text: Mechanical waves transfer energy but not matter: wave properties, the wave equation, sound, reflection and interference, standing waves and resonance. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 11)
meta_desc: Free Physics 11 worksheets (BC Curriculum): wave properties, sound, interference and resonance. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

A wave has amplitude, wavelength (λ), frequency (f) and period (T = 1/f). The universal wave equation is v = fλ. Transverse waves vibrate at right angles to their motion; longitudinal waves such as sound vibrate along it.

When waves meet they interfere: crests that line up add (constructive) and a crest on a trough cancels (destructive). Standing waves form with nodes and antinodes. Resonance happens when an object is pushed at its natural frequency, as in air columns and guitar strings.

Example

A wave has f = 50 Hz and λ = 2.0 m. What is its speed?

v = fλ

Answer: 100 m/s

Example

What kind of wave is sound?

Compressions and rarefactions

Answer: longitudinal

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a higher frequency makes a wave faster in the same medium.
  • Thinking sound can travel in a vacuum.
  • Mixing up amplitude and wavelength.

faq.q: Why does a guitar string make a certain note?
faq.a: It vibrates in standing waves at its natural frequencies.
